monarch_autumn_migration_2026.title: HOW MONARCH BUTTERFLIES FIND THEIR WAY TO MEXICO
monarch_autumn_migration_2026.script: How can a monarch butterfly this fragile travel thousands of miles toward Mexico? Its journey begins when an adult emerges from a chrysalis, ready to feed and fly. That adult feeds on nectar, building the energy needed for a long southbound flight. Sunlight and an internal clock help monarchs hold a heading as the seasons change. This October, observers reported monarchs reaching northern Mexico during the ongoing fall migration. So those tiny wings can lead to Mexico's winter forests, where monarchs sometimes land right on visitors.
monarch_autumn_migration_2026.caption: Monarchs are moving toward Mexico this October. 🦋 #MonarchButterfly #Migration #Wildlife #WildVox

african_penguin_feather_care.title: WHY AFRICAN PENGUINS KEEP COMBING THEIR FEATHERS
african_penguin_feather_care.script: Why does this African penguin keep combing its feathers with its bill? Along southern Africa's coast, these birds move between ocean feeding trips and land. Back ashore, they preen, cleaning and lining up their tightly packed feathers. Their tightly packed feathers help keep cold water away from the skin. But they also need safe places on land where they can shelter and breed. So the constant grooming is more than fussing. It's upkeep for a life split between sea and shore.
african_penguin_feather_care.caption: African penguins have a reason for all that grooming. 🐧 #AfricanPenguin #OceanLife #Wildlife #WildVox

meerkat_lookout_teamwork.title: Why meerkats stand guard for each other
meerkat_lookout_teamwork.script: Why does this meerkat stand upright like a lookout? In the wild, they live in social groups that share space and burrows. One meerkat may stand upright and scan while its neighbors search for food. A lookout can notice approaching danger and give the group time to react. Different individuals can watch their surroundings, helping the group stay alert as it moves. So that famous upright pose is part of teamwork, not just a cute photo.
meerkat_lookout_teamwork.caption: Meerkat lookouts help their groups stay alert. 🐾 #Meerkat #AnimalBehavior #Wildlife #WildVox

african_elephant_mud_bath.title: WHY ELEPHANTS NEED DUST AND WATER BATHS
african_elephant_mud_bath.script: Why do African elephants need both dusty ground and water to stay comfortable? Under the hot African sun, their enormous bodies need ways to shed heat. At a waterhole, elephants wade in, splash, and let water cool their skin. That water helps remove heat, while dust and mud can also protect sensitive skin. And even as a herd moves across dry ground, each elephant still needs ways to cool down. So this isn't just a messy bath. For elephants, it's a way to care for their skin and stay comfortable.
african_elephant_mud_bath.caption: Why African elephants use dust and water to care for their skin. 🐘 #AfricanElephant #Wildlife #AnimalBehavior #WildVox

komodo_dragon_tracking_scent.title: THE SECRET BEHIND A KOMODO DRAGON'S SLOW WALK
komodo_dragon_tracking_scent.script: Why does a Komodo dragon move with such deliberate steps? This enormous monitor lizard lives naturally on a small group of Indonesian islands. Watch the heavy body advance as strong legs and a long tail help it balance. Its forked tongue gathers scent particles, giving it clues about nearby animals. That calm-looking pace can be deceptive: Komodo dragons are powerful hunters and scavengers. So those measured steps belong to a predator constantly exploring its world.
komodo_dragon_tracking_scent.caption: Komodo dragons are much more than giant lizards. 🦎 #KomodoDragon #Reptiles #Wildlife #WildVox
